run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T07:22:36Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is firing because the frontend's checkout requests return HTTP 500, and every failing checkout trace ends inside the shipping service at an outbound HTTP POST that cannot even construct a URI: shipping's span reports 'Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat)))' and shipping's /get-quote returns 'Internal Server Error'. Shipping's error rate stepped off zero at the same sample as frontend's (07:22:36), immediately after Deployment shipping was rolled out at 07:21:16-07:21:23Z; the new ReplicaSet shipping-5ffdc77bc8 carries QUOTE_ADDR="quote:0000" while the replaced ReplicaSet shipping-75d58f5d84 carried QUOTE_ADDR="http://quote:8080". That value has no URI scheme, which is the shape of the InvalidFormat error the shipping client span reports, so the fault originates in the Deployment shipping pod template. Frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and shipping each show their own error spans on this path; no pod crashed or restarted, all flagd fault-injection flags are off, and the quote/email services show no error evidence and simply stop receiving traffic. Two entities outside this path (ad, fraud-detection; plus recommendation) carry small pre-existing error rates that did not change at onset and are background, not impact.

claims.text: Frontend error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) was 0 from the first returned sample at 06:56:36Z through 07:21:36Z, then rose to 0.237 per second at the 07:22:36Z sample (exactly the alert start), 2.19/s at 07:29:36Z and a peak of 2.34/s at 07:30:36Z. This is the deviation the alert reports.

Frontend's error spans are confined to the checkout path. Per span_name, error rate was non-zero only for "POST", "POST /api/checkout", "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" and the client span "grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"; operations GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and tcp.connect stayed at 0.

Trace 5cd2e6d2cf6e511e642b437d77c3a57e shows the error path through explicit parent references: load-generator POST (http.status_code 500) -> frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" and "ingress" (500) -> frontend POST (500) -> frontend "POST /api/checkout" (500) -> frontend "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" (500) -> frontend client span "grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) -> checkout server span "oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) -> checkout internal span "prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart" -> checkout client span "HTTP POST" (error) -> shipping "/get-quote" (error, "Internal Server Error") -> shipping client span "POST " (error, "Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat)))", duration 10us).

Shipping's own server span "/get-quote" carries otel.status_description "Internal Server Error" and completed in 68 microseconds, and its child span "POST " failed in 10 microseconds with otel.status_description "Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat)))"; the shipping container's service_version tag is 2.1.3. The failing outbound POST is therefore rejected before any network round trip.

Checkout reports the propagated gRPC error exactly as "shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500" with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 on span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and the frontend client span carries the same grpc.error_message with "13 INTERNAL:" prefix. No email-service span and no quote-service span appear anywhere in this trace, so the trace does not show a completed call to either service.

Deployment shipping (namespace otel-demo) currently sets container env QUOTE_ADDR="quote:0000" on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-shipping. Comparing the two shipping ReplicaSets: shipping-75d58f5d84 (created 2026-11-17T06:44:45Z, replicas 0) had QUOTE_ADDR="http://quote:8080", while shipping-5ffdc77bc8 (created 2026-11-17T07:21:16Z, replicas 1) has QUOTE_ADDR="quote:0000" and the same image - a configuration-only template change. QUOTE_ADDR is the only outbound-address setting in that container.

Kubernetes events in namespace otel-demo record the rollout: Deployment shipping "Scaled up replica set shipping-5ffdc77bc8 from 0 to 1" at 07:21:16Z and "Scaled down replica set shipping-75d58f5d84 from 1 to 0" at 07:21:23Z; ReplicaSet shipping-5ffdc77bc8 created pod shipping-5ffdc77bc8-755zn and ReplicaSet shipping-75d58f5d84 deleted pod shipping-75d58f5d84-gw77q; the new pod was Scheduled 07:21:16Z, image already present, container shipping Started 07:21:23Z. The rollout precedes the 07:22:36Z error onset and the alert start.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready at query time with container restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason; the only pods with a start time inside the incident window are shipping-5ffdc77bc8-755zn (started 07:21:16Z) - every other pod, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-lmznt, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-6qdxt, checkout-5dccddf8bb-7gfz7, quote-6b5877698d-6spfl and email-59f69bc6cf-zwpwn, started 06:44-06:46Z.

Shipping container logs for 07:20:00-07:36:18Z contain 339 lines, and every one of them is the string "Requesting quote"; a case-insensitive filter for err|error|fail|invalid|uri matched none of those 339 lines. So each request is attempting a quote lookup and the container logs no explanatory error line.

Every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has defaultVariant "off", including adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure; all are "state": "ENABLED" with the off variant selected.

Services quote, shipping and email each expose port 8080 with targetPort 8080 and selectors opentelemetry.io/name=quote|shipping|email, and all three have populated Endpoints (quote 100.96.4.18:8080, shipping 100.96.3.140:8080, email 100.96.4.155:8080), so name resolution targets and backends for the intended callee exist.

Quote and email show only STATUS_CODE_UNSET series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in this window; their span rates decayed from 2.20/s (quote) and 2.93/s (email) at 07:21:00Z to 0 by 07:27:00Z and stayed at 0 through 07:36:00Z - i.e. they stop receiving work once shipping's outbound POST fails, rather than producing errors of their own.
Frontend's own error share was 5.43% at 07:31:00Z, from 2.3735 error spans/s against 41.3325 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans/s on the same service.

The fault originates in the Deployment shipping object: its pod template changed at 07:21:16Z from QUOTE_ADDR="http://quote:8080" to QUOTE_ADDR="quote:0000", and shipping's outbound quote POST then fails with an invalid-URI error in 10us, returning "Internal Server Error" from /get-quote, which propagates as rpc.grpc.status_code 13 to checkout and as HTTP 500 to frontend's POST /api/checkout.

Services outside the checkout path did not step up at 07:22:36Z: ad (about 0.0037/s), fraud-detection (about 0.0037/s) and recommendation (about 0.0037-0.0044/s) all show the same small non-zero error rate both before and after the onset sample, which is pre-existing background rather than impact from this cause. accounting, cart and payment error rates were 0 for every sample in 06:56:36-07:35:36Z.

Rejected: feature-flag fault injection caused the failures. The flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json has every candidate injection flag (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) at defaultVariant "off", and the observed failure is a locally rejected invalid outbound URI rather than a simulated application error.

Rejected: a crash, OOM kill or eviction of the shipping/checkout/frontend pods. All otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason, and the only otel-demo events are Normal Scheduling/Pulling/Created/Started/Killing and SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/ScalingReplicaSet from the deliberate shipping rollout - no OOMKilling, Evicted or Unhealthy events.

Rejected: the quote service failed and thereby broke shipping. quote's pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, the quote Service has a populated Endpoint at 100.96.4.18:8080, no STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series exists for quote, and shipping's failing span lasted 10us with an invalid-URI error, which is too fast and too local to be a response from a remote service.

The exact malformed string is the value itself: shipping's client code derives its request URL from QUOTE_ADDR, and "quote:0000" has no URI scheme (the replaced ReplicaSet used the absolute URL "http://quote:8080"), which would yield a local InvalidFormat parse failure. The span does not print the literal URI, so this reading of the InvalidUri error is inferred from the config difference plus the error class rather than printed directly. Note also that checkout's error text names the email service while the trace shows no email span, so which downstream shipping intended to POST to is not established by a completed call.

Advisory: restore the shipping container's QUOTE_ADDR to the absolute URL the previous ReplicaSet used, http://quote:8080 (quote's Service and Endpoint are on port 8080), through normal change control, then confirm shipping /get-quote returns 200, that quote's span rate returns above 0, and that frontend's error-span rate on POST /api/checkout falls back to 0.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what edited the Deployment shipping pod template at 07:21:16Z (and whether the QUOTE_ADDR value was intentional) could not be determined.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing, and a query for all alert-type rules also returned nothing, so the alert's exact expression and the meaning of the reported value 1.7777777777777777 are unverified.

kube-state-metrics series are not present: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing in the window and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no series, so historical deployment/pod readiness metrics for shipping, quote, email, checkout and frontend could not be checked; pod state is known only from the current API read.

No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned for quote, email, currency, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, product-catalog or quote in the per-service error query, which leaves their error status unknown rather than zero for those services; only quote and email were probed further via their STATUS_CODE_UNSET series.

Shipping's previous container instance does not exist ("previous terminated container shipping ... not found") and the pre-rollout pod shipping-75d58f5d84-gw77q was deleted, so logs from the old configuration cannot be read for comparison.
Shipping logs were read only through 07:30:17Z (the newest 30 of 339 lines were shown, 309 lines omitted), so log content after 07:30:17Z is unread.

A networkpolicy query for namespace otel-demo returned no items (status no_data), so it is not established whether any NetworkPolicy existed at the incident time; the observed error is a local URI parse failure and does not require a network policy explanation.
Whether the quote or email application logs record anything in the window was not examined; their assessment rests on pod state, endpoints and span metrics only.
next_steps: Consult the deployment/CI change history for otel-demo Deployment shipping at 2026-11-17T07:21:16Z to identify who introduced QUOTE_ADDR="quote:0000".
Restore shipping's QUOTE_ADDR to http://quote:8080 via the normal pipeline and verify shipping /get-quote returns 200 and frontend checkout errors stop.
Fetch the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files to confirm which expression produces the reported value.
Add a pre-merge or admission validation that rejects service-address env vars without a scheme or with port 0, so this class of config error is caught before rollout.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
